blocks.text: This chapter presents Josiah’s Passover within the larger account of his reform: repair of the temple leads to the discovery and public reading of the law book, Huldah’s oracle, covenant renewal, removal of abominations, and then this major Passover before Josiah’s death at Megiddo. The sequence frames the celebration as part of the king’s wider response to the law.

Chronicles recounts Neco’s warning to Josiah and says that Josiah did not listen to words “from the mouth of God.” Kings also reports Josiah’s death at Megiddo, but without this speech explaining his decision. The two accounts should therefore be read with their distinct wording and aims in view, rather than silently importing the explanation from one into the other.

Verse 25 says that Jeremiah lamented for Josiah. The later attribution of Lamentations to Jeremiah is an ancient reception tradition, supported by Greek paratext and the books’ canonical proximity, rather than an explicit claim of the Hebrew text itself.
